kind: Prospective hosted native protocol screen, 197 unchanged originals plus4separately corrected explicit-React candidates; not blind new designs
retry_policy: one CLI process per selected case, serial, no retries; preserve every first failure
constraints: No API admission-policy changes or API requests; native session directives and every observation retained.
Do not shorten simulated durations to satisfy API limits.
Transport/duration/output resource refusals are not scientific failures or passes.
Zero exit and complete JSON ingestion are engineering outcomes; compare saved physical forecasts separately.
No local VPS native execution or compilation.
Isolated workflow ref must never merge.

cases.physical_forecast: The sample consumes about 2 mmol more acid than the blank, corresponding to 1 mmol CaCO3; silica is excluded from neutralising capacity.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Blank minus sample base demand is close to 2 mmol, allowing two burette increments and residual dissolved CO2.
Recovered carbonate amount agrees with the introduced amount; silica remains a separate inventory.

cases.physical_forecast: The spiked aliquot should require approximately 0.5 mmol more hydroxide, despite a disproportionate change in its starting pH.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Subtracting endpoint doses recovers the 0.5 mmol spike within step-size and endpoint corrections.
Total acetate is conserved in both aliquots.

cases.physical_forecast: The remaining stock and withdrawn aliquot contain approximately 1.5 and 0.5 mmol acid. Their pre-titration concentrations should agree.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Endpoint base demands are approximately 3:1.
Base demand divided by each measured pre-titration volume agrees within dosing resolution.

cases.physical_forecast: The first endpoint requires roughly 0.3 mmol acid and cumulative acid near the second roughly 1.0 mmol. Ideal reconstruction gives n(carbonate)=P and n(bicarbonate)=T−2P.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Save first-stage and additional second-stage doses separately; cumulative T includes both.
The reconstructed amounts are nonnegative and approximate the 0.3/0.4 mmol inputs.

cases.physical_forecast: Approximately 0.5 mmol BaSO4 should be retained, while chloride-rich solution passes into the filtrate; the precipitate is not the total salt mass.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use the BaSO4 solid inventory to infer 0.5 mmol sulfate, not the mass of the whole wet vessel.
Chloride remains predominantly in the filtrate and contributes no sulfate-equivalent precipitate.

cases.physical_forecast: The ideal equivalence volume is 10.35 mL. A whole-step endpoint is expected near 11 mL for 1 mL steps and 10.4 mL for 0.1 mL steps, unless the engine explicitly interpolates.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare actual delivered volumes with the 10.35 mL stoichiometric reference.
Distinguish an interpolated estimate from the physical amount actually added.

cases.physical_forecast: The calcium-chloride spike introduces 0.4 mmol chloride, so the spiked arm should retain approximately 0.4 mmol more AgCl, not 0.2 mmol.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Subtract solid AgCl inventories to recover two chloride ions per CaCl2 unit.
Neither arm should be silver-limited at the specified amounts.

cases.physical_forecast: The weak/weak system changes pH more gradually across equal formal equivalents than the strong/strong control, although proton transfer occurs in both.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare the pH span from 80% to 120% equivalents for the two systems.
Both weak-acid and weak-base analytical pools remain accounted for after neutralisation.

cases.physical_forecast: The suspension can replenish dissolved hydroxide by consuming solid Mg(OH)2. Its filtrate lacks that reserve and should acidify much more under the same acid dose.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Initial dissolved-state pH values are compared before the challenge.
Acid causes loss of hydroxide solid in v1 while the isolated filtrate becomes substantially more acidic.

cases.physical_forecast: Acid additions consume carbonate and release inorganic carbon before a strong-acid excess appears. The final 2.5 mmol total acid exceeds the 2 mmol ideal solid capacity.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Track solid consumption and carbon transfer through the sequence.
The final state reflects exhausted carbonate and an acid-equivalent excess, rather than indefinite buffering.

cases.physical_forecast: Methyl orange changes in an acidic region and cannot uniquely mark acetic-acid equivalence. Phenolphthalein is responsive in the alkaline region near this titration endpoint.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Relate each colour to the simultaneous pH rather than to the same fractional dose.
Indicator inventories remain trace compared with the acid/base pool.

cases.physical_forecast: Bromothymol-blue colour should follow acid–base reversals while the indicator amount is retained; neutralisation changes its environment rather than repeatedly creating dye.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Acidic snapshots have consistent indicator response and differ from the alkaline snapshot.
The indicator analytical amount is conserved through all three states.

cases.physical_forecast: Acid favours CO2/carbonic-acid forms, whereas base favours carbonate. The same initial bicarbonate pool therefore displays both sides of amphiprotic behaviour.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare carbon species distributions as well as pH.
The acid arm has a different gas-phase carbon allocation while both closed total carbon budgets remain 1 mmol.

cases.physical_forecast: Both calcium compounds have an ideal capacity of 1 mmol H+ at this loading, but only carbonate supplies 0.5 mmol inorganic carbon and the associated CO2 response.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Calcium and residual acid-equivalent budgets are compared independently of gas production.
The oxide arm must not acquire carbon or emit an invented carbonate gas.

cases.physical_forecast: Heating chloride hardness does not supply carbonate. Soda treatment can remove calcium as a carbonate-bearing solid; boiling alone mainly changes water and concentration.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Calcium in the heated arm is not falsely removed as CaCO3 without a carbon source.
The treated filtrate is depleted in calcium relative to its feed.

cases.physical_forecast: Initially, added water dissolves excess halite and the solution remains near saturation. After the solid reservoir is exhausted, further dilution lowers concentration more directly.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Track decreasing solid NaCl before expecting large concentration dilution.
Distinguish saturated activity/concentration from nonlinearly responding conductivity.

cases.physical_forecast: With solid metal present in both zinc half-cells, their equilibrium potentials should be similar despite different metal reserves.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare cell voltages alongside Zn2+ activities and temperatures.
Reading voltage does not consume the larger or smaller electrode.

cases.physical_forecast: Cumulative copper metal deposition cannot substantially exceed the 0.5 mmol zinc electron-donor budget; later copper additions increasingly remain dissolved.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Sum zinc oxidation and copper reduction across all doses.
Residual Cu2+ after the final dose is not misreported as a lack of initial reaction.

cases.physical_forecast: Ferric iron can oxidise iodide; ferrous iron is not an equivalent oxidant. Total iron concentration alone does not determine redox capacity.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Link iodine production to Fe(III) reduction rather than merely to iron colour.
Check dissolved oxygen or other oxidants before interpreting the ferrous arm.

cases.physical_forecast: Both commands deliver 5 C. At equal modelled current efficiency their incremental hydrogen and oxygen products should agree.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare generated gas increments after subtracting initial headspace inventory.
Use total charge and reported efficiencies; current alone is not the product prediction.

cases.physical_forecast: An open-boundary dose can lose carbon before sealing; a closed dose retains its carbon budget. Final states need not agree even with identical nominal additions.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Account explicitly for carbon transferred out before the first vessel was sealed.
Sealing must not restore previously lost carbon.

cases.physical_forecast: Initial CO2 is strongly absorbed as carbonate/bicarbonate. As alkalinity is spent, more added carbon remains as dissolved CO2 and headspace gas.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Relate changing gas allocation to the carbonate/bicarbonate inventory and falling pH.
Do not assume a single sharp 2 OH:1 CO2 capacity after bicarbonate becomes important.

cases.physical_forecast: The initial acid dose can convert carbonate mainly toward bicarbonate while already liberating more CO2 from the bicarbonate arm. With excess acid, both contain the same original carbon budget.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare initial CO2 allocation rather than total pressure alone.
Final retained carbon across phases remains 1 mmol per closed vessel.

cases.physical_forecast: Peroxide consumption should accelerate after catalyst introduction, relative to the initial uncatalysed interval.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Calculate interval consumption from inventories, allowing unequal remaining substrate.
MnO2 must not be consumed as a stoichiometric fuel.

cases.physical_forecast: The catalyst-free filtrate should consume less additional peroxide than the unfiltered control, after correcting for their inventories at filtration.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Record the post-filtration starting peroxide in v3.
Distinguish slowed uncatalysed reaction from a claim of absolutely zero decomposition.

cases.physical_forecast: The dilute naphthalene can pass the filter but favour the hexane extract, whereas the ionic salt remains mainly aqueous.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm that naphthalene was dissolved before filtration.
Track sodium/chloride and naphthalene separately through extraction.

cases.physical_forecast: A filter first passes dissolved nitrate solution; cooling the filtrate can produce crystals that a second filtration then retains.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify dissolved and solid KNO3 at both filtration steps.
Calculate crystal recovery from phase inventories, not from total vessel mass alone.

cases.physical_forecast: Under ideal homogeneous liquid withdrawal, three 80% decants leave about 0.2^3=0.008 of the original dissolved salt with the retained solid.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare remaining sodium/chloride with the geometric reference.
Sum salt over every wash fraction and verify silica retention.

cases.physical_forecast: Sodium chloride is largely rejected by distillation, while a represented volatile acetic-acid fraction can enter the condensate and affect its pH.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify acid in v4 rather than inferring it solely from low pH.
Compare nonvolatile sodium/chloride carryover with the volatile acid budget.

cases.physical_forecast: A lower aqueous fraction, an organic liquid fraction and an insoluble solid residue should be distinguishable, subject to the operators’ actual phase semantics.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify the composition of each destination rather than assigning it from vessel number.
Close water, hexane, salt and silica balances across all three vessels.

cases.physical_forecast: The model’s ferromagnetic solid operation should collect metallic iron, not remove dissolved Fe(III) merely because the element is iron.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare metallic and dissolved iron transfer independently.
A magnetic susceptibility concept must not be confused with bulk extraction of all iron ions.

cases.physical_forecast: Clarified silica remains as a solid sediment, whereas dissolved salt remains in the liquid. Both may present a clear liquid layer for different reasons.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use phase-resolved inventories to distinguish sediment from dissolved solute.
Do not infer chemical disappearance from reduced turbidity.

cases.physical_forecast: Both mixtures can neutralise approximately 0.0005 mol of hydroxide, so the neutralisation contribution should be similar rather than doubled. The second mixture retains more excess acid.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Calculate temperature changes against each pair of measured pre-mixing temperatures and heat capacities.
Confirm the same hydroxide consumption but different residual acidity.

cases.physical_forecast: Both portions can remain near the melting temperature while the more strongly cooled portion contains more ice and a lower retained enthalpy.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm coexistence of ice and liquid before comparing equal temperatures.
Use the different phase fractions and known cooling inputs to explain why temperature alone does not determine stored energy.

cases.physical_forecast: Both arms can neutralise 0.001 mol, but the less dilute arm should show the larger mixing-corrected temperature rise because it has a smaller thermal mass.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare heat-capacity-weighted pre-mixing baselines with final temperatures.
Distinguish approximately equal neutralisation energy from unequal temperature changes; do not demand an exact fourfold ratio.

cases.physical_forecast: At a common wavelength and optical path, a dilute nonreacting copper chromophore should show falling absorbance as concentration decreases, while total copper remains constant.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use reported actual volumes and species concentrations, not an assumed volume convention for dilute.
Compare the same spectral feature and check for complexation or precipitation before fitting a linear dilution relation.

cases.physical_forecast: The silica solid should be retained while dissolved copper largely follows the liquid. A scattering-aware optical model may show improved clarity without disappearance of copper absorption.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Resolve silica retention and copper transfer separately in the material balance.
Distinguish a missing scattering model from an actual absence of solid particles in the starting sample.

cases.physical_forecast: Both treatments can weaken iodine-family colour, but dilution preserves oxidised-iodine equivalents while ascorbic acid can reduce iodine to iodide. The spectral changes need not be numerically equal.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare oxidised-iodine equivalents across I2 and I3- rather than interpreting either individual species alone.
Reconcile total iodine in both arms and identify oxidation of the reducing agent only in the chemical arm.

cases.physical_forecast: First-endpoint demand P should be near 0.7 mmol and total T near 1.0 mmol. Ideal reconstruction gives n(OH)=2P−T and n(CO3)=T−P.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The first endpoint accounts for more than half of total alkalinity.
The reconstructed hydroxide/carbonate quantities approximate 0.4/0.3 mmol.

cases.physical_forecast: The stoichiometric requirement is 0.4 mmol permanganate, corresponding to 20 mL of the nominal 0.02 M titrant; a small persistent excess defines the endpoint.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Cumulative titrant volume brackets 20 mL with the chosen 0.2 mL step, subject to model response.
Inspect both oxalate depletion and persistent oxidant; a generic colour event is insufficient.

cases.physical_forecast: The ideal endpoint is at a cumulative 0.2 mmol thiosulfate. An endpoint interval, rather than a falsely exact titre, follows from the final dose increments.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Iodine-equivalent inventory decreases with each thiosulfate dose and is exhausted near 0.2 mmol.
The additional 0.02 mmol is recorded as excess reductant rather than extra iodine removal.

cases.physical_forecast: After 0.4 mmol thiosulfate, the vitamin-C arm should be near iodine exhaustion while the blank retains about 0.1 mmol iodine equivalents. Their difference represents 0.1 mmol vitamin C.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The two arms differ by 0.2 mmol thiosulfate-equivalent demand.
Carbon and iodine balances support reduction rather than a colour-only artefact.

cases.physical_forecast: The pH-seven stop generally occurs before the weak-acid equivalence region. The higher endpoint requires more base; the difference is endpoint bias, not different acid content.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Both acid inputs are equal, but saved endpoint doses differ in the expected direction.
Infer bias from actual delivered doses, not from the target pH numbers alone.

cases.physical_forecast: Both routes target 1 mmol acetic acid, 1 mmol acetate, 2 mmol sodium and 1 mmol chloride. Their pH should be similar after accounting for temperature and small water differences.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare analytical acetate, sodium and chloride budgets before comparing pH.
Any pH difference is assessed against temperature and reaction-water differences rather than attributed to bottle order alone.

cases.physical_forecast: Acid/base recharge approximately restores the buffer ratio while sodium/chloride accumulate. Similar pH values need not imply identical conductivity or ionic strength.

acceptance_checks.criterion: The acetate pool remains constant through both cycles.
Final sodium and chloride increments equal the added strong acid/base budgets; conductivity is evaluated independently of pH recovery.

cases.physical_forecast: Selective NH3 removal should deplete the base component and lower pH relative to the sealed control; the ammonium/chloride reservoir is not itself a gas.

acceptance_checks.criterion: A pH decrease is accompanied by a documented loss of nitrogen through the gas boundary.
Chloride remains retained and is not confused with volatile NH3.

cases.physical_forecast: One equivalent predominantly gives dihydrogen phosphate; two give hydrogen phosphate; a further half equivalent probes the third, high-pH region. These are different species distributions, not the same neutral salt.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use solved phosphate species to interpret each pH, rather than assigning every neutralised salt pH seven.
Total phosphorus is 1 mmol in each vessel.

cases.physical_forecast: Thiocyanate should increase the complex-bound iron fraction and its characteristic optical response without introducing more iron.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Require an explicitly identified Fe–SCN complex; a mixed colour alone does not establish complexation.
Total Fe remains 0.1 mmol.

cases.physical_forecast: AgCl should tend to convert to AgI while chloride is released, if both phases and their exchange equilibrium are represented.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify loss of AgCl and formation of AgI, not merely a colour change.
Silver across retained solid and filtrate does not increase during exchange.

cases.physical_forecast: The first stage preferentially retains magnesium hydroxide; the subsequent carbonate stage targets calcium in the first filtrate.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Quantify Ca and Mg in both solid fractions and final solution.
Do not call the separation quantitative without reporting cross-contamination.

cases.physical_forecast: A modest chloride-containing rinse should reduce AgCl dissolution relative to a pure-water rinse, while both remove soluble impurities.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare Ag losses in the second filtrates v5 and v6.
Include silver already lost in the first filtration when calculating total recovery.

cases.physical_forecast: Sulfate should strongly compete for barium. Only after sufficient barium is available can substantial carbonate precipitation coexist; neither anion may consume the same barium twice.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Sum barium in every solid and aqueous species against its input.
Compare phase allocation in the barium-deficient and barium-excess-to-sulfate arms.

cases.physical_forecast: The acetate-buffered arm spends hydroxide on its acid reserve, delaying extensive copper hydroxide precipitation compared with the unbuffered arm.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Separate base spent on acetate protonation from the formal 2 OH per Cu precipitation budget.
Later base addition should change pH and phase allocation, not create extra copper.

cases.physical_forecast: A calcium-phosphate-bearing solid may capture phosphorus from solution; acidification of the isolated solid should favour dissolved phosphate species.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify the actual calcium phosphate phase and track total phosphorus through filtration.
Dissolution must release phosphorus from the retained solid, not merely change liquid pH.

cases.physical_forecast: Signed differences should satisfy E13≈E12+E23 when each reading uses the same half-cell states and convention.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use signed, consistently oriented voltages, not their absolute values.
Verify no intervening cell measurement changes inventories.

cases.physical_forecast: An ideal concentration-ratio model predicts little change because both concentrations fall together; real activity and complexation corrections can produce a residual shift.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Reconstruct the prediction using solved Cu2+/Zn2+ activity ratios.
Do not label every nonzero voltage shift a failure of the Nernst relation.

cases.physical_forecast: AgCl precipitation lowers free Ag+ activity in one half-cell and can create a concentration-related voltage while both contain silver metal.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Require an AgCl phase and a lowered free-Ag+ activity in the treated half-cell.
Distinguish sign convention from the existence of a potential difference.

cases.physical_forecast: Reduction of available silver can draw further AgCl dissolution, yielding silver metal and dissolved zinc/chloride if the coupled phases are represented.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Require Ag metal formation with corresponding AgCl loss and Zn oxidation.
At most 0.4 mmol Ag originates from the introduced silver salt.

cases.physical_forecast: For the acidic Mn2+ endpoint, 1 mmol Fe(II) supplies the electrons for 0.2 mmol permanganate, nominally 10 mL titrant.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm Fe(II) loss, Fe(III) formation and the actual manganese endpoint.
Do not apply the 5:1 ratio if MnO2 or another manganese product dominates.

cases.physical_forecast: Copper recovered from zinc displacement can reduce silver ions in a second stage. The interpretation depends on confirming that residual zinc is not the direct silver donor.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Inspect the first retained solid for residual Zn before attributing silver deposition to copper.
Track Cu oxidation and Ag reduction in a 1:2 electron ratio where copper is the donor.

cases.physical_forecast: The 0.05 mmol copper inventory can accept only about 9.65 C for complete Cu(II)-to-Cu reduction. Further charge cannot create more copper than supplied.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Total deposited copper stays within the initial copper budget unless an explicitly modelled copper anode supplies more.
Identify the later cathodic product or an explicit refusal after Cu depletion.

cases.physical_forecast: Base favours NH3; subsequent acid returns nitrogen toward ammonium and lowers its gas-phase share without removing total nitrogen.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Track NH3 gas separately from ammonium and dissolved ammonia.
Nitrogen is conserved through the closed acid–base cycle.

cases.physical_forecast: Warming changes gas pressure and CO2 partitioning. Cooling toward the original temperature should approximately restore the partition without needing a new carbon dose.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Closed total carbon remains constant throughout.
Judge recovery at the actual returned temperature, allowing modelled thermal effects.

cases.physical_forecast: The larger water volume should hold a larger fraction of the finite carbon dose, reducing its gas-phase pressure contribution relative to the small-water arm.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare CO2 gas moles and dissolved carbon moles, not only total pressure.
Both arms have identical introduced carbon and headspace volume.

cases.physical_forecast: The requested overall route consumes 6 O2 and forms 6 CO2 per glucose. Gas pressure need not be unchanged because CO2 and O2 partition differently and water is also formed.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify glucose-derived carbon and oxygen consumption before interpreting pressure.
Compare gas-only changes with liquid-plus-gas budgets.

cases.physical_forecast: Captured carbonate carbon should remain with the isolated solid and reappear as CO2/dissolved carbon on acidification; uncaptured carbon stays in the earlier liquid/gas accounts.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Quantify carbon in the first solid before assigning recaptured gas to it.
Sum carbon over both vessels and any boundary transfer during filtration.

cases.physical_forecast: For the same material and spherical-particle approximation, mass/diameter is matched, so the two nominal surface-controlled responses should be similar.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare fractional substrate consumption at the same elapsed times.
Confirm that catalyst activity uses the stated diameters rather than defaults.

cases.physical_forecast: Reducing particle size should increase subsequent surface-mediated consumption. The grind command itself must not retrospectively generate the previous interval’s extra products.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare the snapshot immediately before and after grinding.
Interpret later rates using the remaining peroxide and unchanged catalyst mass.

cases.physical_forecast: If enzyme and substrate transfer proportionally, both portions retain the same concentrations and should show similar fractional peroxide depletion, while absolute consumption scales with volume.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify proportional enzyme and substrate transfer before comparing rates.
Compare fractional loss from each post-split starting amount, not equal absolute gas amounts.

cases.physical_forecast: At matched catalyst activity and temperature, a first-order surface teaching model predicts similar fractions remaining, despite different absolute initial substrate.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Normalise each peroxide trace by its own initial amount.
Test logarithmic decay only over an interval with approximately stable temperature and catalyst activity.

cases.physical_forecast: Cooling should lower the rate coefficient of the ongoing MnO2/peroxide model, separate from the decline caused by substrate depletion.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Use measured temperatures and remaining substrate to compare apparent rate coefficients.
Catalyst mass remains constant.

cases.physical_forecast: Base removes available acidity and should strongly suppress further sulfur formation; renewed acid can restart conversion of remaining thiosulfate.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare sulfur increments before quench, during quench and after re-acidification.
Track acid consumption by both reaction and neutralisation.

cases.physical_forecast: If acid and thiosulfate remain in the filtrate, fresh sulfur can form there after the original solid is retained in the first vessel.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify residual acid/thiosulfate in v2 immediately after filtration.
New solid in v2 must be distinguished from transferred old sulfur.

cases.physical_forecast: If the first route produces MnO2, its isolated solid should accelerate peroxide decomposition relative to the catalyst-free control.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Confirm MnO2 formation and isolation before assigning catalytic action.
Exclude residual permanganate as a stoichiometric oxidant in the second stage.

cases.physical_forecast: Reduction should convert extractable iodine into more water-favouring iodide, enabling reactive back-extraction into the newly added aqueous phase.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Track iodine atoms across original raffinate, organic extract and stripping water.
Require iodide formation rather than attributing every colour loss to phase transfer.

cases.physical_forecast: At equal radius, ideal centrifugal acceleration scales as rpm squared; the higher-speed arm should show greater settling if the model resolves the regime.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare reported acceleration or settling fraction, not a presumed fourfold final pellet mass.
Total silica remains conserved in each vessel.

cases.physical_forecast: Larger particles should settle more readily in a dilute Stokes-like regime; equal solid mass does not imply equal separation speed.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify that particle-size metadata reaches the sedimentation calculation.
Do not claim a universal hundredfold yield ratio from a diameter-squared velocity law.

cases.physical_forecast: Cooling should favour potassium-nitrate crystallisation while the smaller sodium-chloride charge may remain largely in solution.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Calculate the KNO3-to-NaCl ratio in retained solids and compare with the feed.
Distinguish purity improvement from complete nitrate recovery.

cases.physical_forecast: At matched composition and phase-volume ratio, an ideal dilute partition model predicts similar fractional naphthalene recovery despite a twofold batch scale.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare extracted fraction of each initial naphthalene dose, not equal extracted moles.
Verify both feeds are below aqueous saturation.

cases.physical_forecast: If both routes reach the same retained composition without different losses, their complete-route enthalpy balances should agree. Intermediate heat changes differ because hydration and neutralisation are separated in the second route.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare full-route energy ledgers from the same initial inputs, not only the final command increment.
Verify final phase and species inventories match before interpreting a Hess-law comparison.

cases.physical_forecast: Warm water first supplies sensible and latent energy to the cold portion. The final temperature should fall below a liquid-only weighted-temperature prediction when initial ice is present.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Read the actual initial ice fraction and temperature before estimating a fusion energy.
Close the energy balance including warming any sub-zero solid and the measured final liquid.

cases.physical_forecast: An ice-excluding salt model predicts enriched brine in the filtrate and a lower-salt melt from the retained ice. Compare concentrations after accounting for different water masses.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify that ice is actually present and that filtration separates the intended solid and liquid pools.
Reconcile sodium and chloride across both vessels; compare salinity at matched temperature or with a temperature correction.

cases.physical_forecast: A pressure-aware phase model predicts a higher water boiling temperature at 2 bar and a different sensible-versus-latent allocation of the same heat.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Check actual pressure and phase inventories rather than assuming the regulator has no mass exchange.
Compare any reported boiling points with the operative vessel pressure, not automatically with a 1 bar reference value.

cases.physical_forecast: Equal-mass samples have different temperature rises. For these metals near room temperature, the equal-mole comparison is expected to be closer because molar heat capacities are more similar than mass-specific values.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Infer heat capacities using each sample mass or mole amount and observed temperature rise.
Treat approximate similarity of molar heat capacities as a material-dependent trend, not an exact identity.

cases.physical_forecast: When supported by the coupled brine/ice model, salt lowers the freezing equilibrium temperature and promotes melting that consumes latent energy. Cooling and melting can therefore occur together.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare both temperature and ice fraction before and after salt addition.
Include salt dissolution energy and any undissolved salt in the interpretation, rather than attributing every joule to freezing-point depression.

cases.physical_forecast: If only the requested first arm esterifies, its remaining acid demand should be lower than the unactivated feed control. The titration-derived difference should be checked against the pre-workup ester inventory.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare delivered hydroxide equivalents and separately inspect the acid and ester pools before dilution.
Check whether dilution or titration causes further hydrolysis; do not interpret that extra reaction as original conversion.

cases.physical_forecast: The activated arm should generate titratable acetic acid in proportion to ethanol converted. The unactivated arm tests whether an explicit named reaction is required.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Relate the blank-corrected base demand to the observed ethanol loss and acetate-family gain.
Account for any oxygen initially present in the sealed headspace instead of equating explicit oxygen addition with the entire oxygen budget.

cases.physical_forecast: The requested respiration can release up to 0.0006 mol of carbon dioxide from this glucose dose. Lime addition may transfer some of that carbon into carbonate solid while the rest remains in dissolved or gaseous pools.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Account for all six carbons per converted glucose across every retained carbon-bearing pool.
Identify carbonate separately from any excess unreacted calcium hydroxide before using retained solid mass as a carbon assay.

cases.physical_forecast: For complete hydrolysis, the activated sample should consume about 0.0005 mol less strong acid than the base blank at an endpoint that mostly leaves acetate deprotonated.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare the blank-minus-sample delivered acid equivalents with the observed ester loss.
Correct for endpoint resolution and check that appreciable acetate protonation or incomplete hydrolysis does not bias the difference.

cases.physical_forecast: A temperature-dependent transport model can change conductivity during warming even though sodium and chloride totals are unchanged. Cooling tests reversibility rather than chemical consumption.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify constant retained salt totals and inspect any water loss or volume change.
Identify whether the instrument reports temperature-compensated or in-situ conductivity before interpreting the sign and magnitude.

cases.physical_forecast: If the chromatograph recognises the relevant molecular pools, ester features should decrease and ethanol features increase as additional hydroxide permits further hydrolysis.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Relate peak identities to independently reported species inventories after each stage.
Do not compare raw areas as stoichiometric mole ratios unless response factors are provided; ionic acetate need not produce a comparable volatile peak.

cases.physical_forecast: The mixed acetate/phosphate sample should retain an additional buffering region after the acetate-only sample approaches exhaustion.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify buffering intervals from incremental pH changes, not from an assumed common starting pH.
Account separately for all phosphate proton-equivalent steps and for acetate.

cases.physical_forecast: Under a dominant 1:1 FeSCN model, the complex-specific response should peak near the equal-mole mixture, not at the largest iron input.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare complex-specific concentrations or baseline-corrected spectral features, not total colour intensity.
The sum of analytical Fe and SCN is constant across all three samples.

cases.physical_forecast: Phosphate may decrease the Fe–SCN fraction through competing aqueous or solid species; the extra-acid arm helps reveal whether acidity alone explains the response.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify where iron goes when the Fe–SCN response changes.
Do not claim ligand competition solely from unequal pH or a weaker colour.

cases.physical_forecast: Acid destabilises a carbonate-bearing silver solid while AgCl is comparatively retained; liberated silver may redistribute according to chloride availability.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify carbonate-bearing solids before acid addition; absence of such a phase makes the test inconclusive.
Account for silver redistribution and carbon loss rather than expecting a fixed final precipitate mass.

cases.physical_forecast: A salt-induced activity-coefficient change can shift the predicted cell voltage even with unchanged analytical copper and zinc amounts.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare the voltage change with the actual solved free-ion activities.
Do not prescribe a shift direction without those activities.

cases.physical_forecast: The combined-catalyst response must follow an explicit pathway-combination rule; multiplying two observed acceleration factors is not a justified chemical prediction.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Report the three measured conversion fractions and the engine’s stated combination rule.
All arms conserve catalyst and substrate-derived atoms; do not force an unsupported additive or multiplicative claim.

cases.physical_forecast: A larger thiosulfate sink can delay iodine accumulation even if the underlying iodine-production kinetics are similar.
